text: Several projects set out to uncover how animals tell direction from the planet's magnetic field. How do these projects differ in the animal each chose to work with and in which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up?
reference_answer: The four projects split by study animal and by which proposed physical mechanism they set out to test. QuantumBirds works on night-migratory songbirds and set out to prove whether detection happens in the retina through the quantum spin dynamics of photochemically formed radical pairs in cryptochrome proteins. MagneticMoth uses the Australian Bogong moth, aiming to decide between the two contending hypotheses and targeting photoreceptor-based cryptochrome (Cry) molecules in the eyes, having cloned genes for 4 visual opsins and 2 Cry. NeuroMag uses pigeons as a model system and asks whether the primary sensors are inner ear hair cells and whether detection depends on magnetic crystals (magnetite) or on electromagnetic induction, while NeuroMagMa takes mole-rats, a rodent living in darkness underground, and pursues the magnetite theory plus magnetic input to head direction cells.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-50 (sample_ids 810002, 741298, 948728); drift re-run of the seed SQL returned 4 rows, adding 819336 NeuroMag, so all four are seeds/gold. All four read in full (objective + report teaser/summary) before the question was drafted. FIX ROUND 1 reworded the second comparison dimension from 'the physical explanation each set out to test' (singular) to 'which candidate physical mechanism or mechanisms each set out to weigh up', because 819336 ('whether ... magnetic crystals or electromagnetic induction', three candidate ideas in its report summary) and 741298 ('isolating which of the two current (contentious) hypotheses ... apply') set out to adjudicate between mechanisms rather than test one; naming one mechanism for 810002/948728 and two for 819336/741298 is now equally admissible. Pooled adjudication re-run on the reworded text at k=10 (19 distinct projects): IN 741298 (dense 1, hybrid 5, rerank 4), 819336 (dense 2, hybrid 10, rerank 3), 948728 (hybrid 1, rerank 2, dense 3, lexical 4), 810002 (dense 8, rerank 8). OUT: 817535 UltimateCOMPASS (dung-beetle 'snapshot compass' on celestial cues, no magnetic field), 743093 ElectroBee (aerial electroreception of electric, not magnetic, fields), 679086 COMPASS (spacecraft orbit control), 864792 OXYGEN (arc magma geochemistry), 852086 AGEMEC (Alzheimer's neurons), and 10 planetary/stellar magnetism projects (893304 SIGMA, 815559 MHDiscs, 948582 IMAGINE, 833848 UEMHP, 844252 PETRA, 748544 DiskTorqueOnPlanets, 679937 MagneticYSOs, 890962 MarsMag, 101030103 REVErSI, 740651 NewWorlds) - none concern animal sensing. Completeness sweep (run_sql over project.objective/title: magnetorecept, magnetic sense, magnetic compass, magnetic orientation, geomagnetic, magnetosens, magnetic sens in title, and magnetic field AND (navigat|orientation|migrat)) returned 48 projects; the only animal-magnetic-sensing members are the four gold. Bacterial magnetism projects (692637 SYNTOMAGX, 797431 BioNanoMagnets) are magnetotactic bacteria, not animals orienting, and are OUT. The independent critic additionally swept two alternative vocabularies and the report text (teaser+summary+workPerformed+finalResults) and found no fifth animal magnetic-sensing project, its only non-gold hit being 899792 MagFlow, a magnetically steered microcatheter. term_style=paraphrase: the question avoids the gold texts' own words (magnetoreception, magnetic sense, compass, cryptochrome, radical pair, magnetite, Earth's magnetic field); on the reworded text three of the four gold projects have no lexical rank at all and lexical's top slots are astrophysics. Membership is worded as what each project SET OUT to do, so partial or pivoted execution does not change the gold set.

text: What do EU-funded projects on cancer cachexia identify as the drivers of the wasting of adipose tissue and muscle in cancer patients?
reference_answer: Two projects study cancer cachexia head-on and together describe it as a whole-body failure rather than a muscle-local one. CSI-Fun treats cancer associated cachexia (CAC) as a disorder of the whole body affecting 50-80% of cancer patients and the immediate cause of death for a third of them, and demonstrated experimentally that uncontrolled inflammation and the beta-adrenergic system are important players, with immune cells interacting with the sympathetic nervous system during CAC. StopWaste locates the driver in metabolism: its data support the concept that tumours activate futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, and the project identified cachexia-specific bioreactive lipids stemming from altered liver lipids and dysregulated liver lipid enzymes, which could be targeted with the ceramide synthesis inhibitor myriocin, plus an altered flux of fatty acids and amino acids through the tricarboxylic acid cycle (TCA) in cachectic adipose tissue, partly linked to the TCA gatekeeper PDK4. Combining them, the wasting of fat and muscle is driven by inflammation and neuro-endocrine signalling acting on a reprogrammed lipid and glucose metabolism spanning tumour, adipose tissue and liver, with disturbed glucose metabolism appearing early - patients with disturbed glucose metabolism showed a higher incidence of cachexia associated with pancreatic and colorectal cancers.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile candidate vector-65 (cachexia). Drift check: `SELECT p.id, p.acronym FROM project p WHERE p.objective ILIKE '%cachexia%' OR p.title ILIKE '%cachexia%'` -> 4 rows (683658 LIFEOMEGA, 741888 CSI-Fun, 897735 REBOOST, 949017 StopWaste), matching the candidate. Read all four: 949017 IN (cachexia is the whole project - futile substrate cycling in adipocytes, ceramides, PDK4); 741888 IN (Cancer associated Cachexia is one of its three named research strands, with mechanism findings on inflammation, the beta-adrenergic system and the sympathetic nervous system); 683658 LIFEOMEGA OUT (an omega-3 EPA food-supplement feasibility study; cachexia named only as a target market for clinical nutrition, no investigation of what drives wasting); 897735 REBOOST OUT (SEPN1-related myopathy; cancer cachexia named once as a condition the model paradigm might later extend to). The gold boundary is drawn on what the question asks - the drivers of the wasting of ADIPOSE TISSUE and MUSCLE - not on whether a project mentions or even works on cachexia. Pooled adjudications on the 19-project pool for the final question text: 818943 UreaCa OUT, and this is the closest call, so the ground is stated exactly. UreaCa's cachexia work is NOT incidental - it is a headline outcome of the project: finalResults report that 're-expressing HNF4a restricted tumor growth and the development of cachexia manifestations' and that 'our results, supported by ERC-PoC, led to a patent and the establishment of a new company - Metabocure, which will evaluate the potential benefit of mRNA of HNF4a delivered via lipid nanoparticles in alleviating cancer cachexia in mice and human'. It is excluded because across its ENTIRE stored text (objective, summary, workPerformed, finalResults, teaser) UreaCa speaks only of whole-organism 'cachexia manifestations' and 'cachexia symptoms' and never localises its HNF4a / liver-metabolism driver to adipose tissue or muscle, which is the tissue-level account this question asks for; a re-deriver who reads the finalResults should therefore not be surprised into reopening the boundary. 677006 CMIL OUT on the cancer/infection split, not on topical absence: CMIL does study cachexia in adipose and muscle tissue ('we became interested into systemic immunometabolic changes and took a particular focus on adipose and muscle tissue'), but the cachexia it experimentally drives and models is infection-associated - 'T cell responses mediate cachexia during viral infection and established a novel model to study infection-associated cachexia' - whereas the question asks about cancer patients. 639548 STARS OUT - thyroid-hormone-driven skeletal muscle wasting across chronic diseases, muscle only, not adipose and not cachexia-targeted; 101033310 Myo_LysoZOOM OUT - lysosomal signalling in muscle wasting generally; 694677 VitruVius OUT - Drosophila growth coordination, host tissue wasting only noted as 'similar to' cancer-induced cachexia; 787041 LIPOMET OUT - lists cancer-associated cachexia as an open future question, no findings; 101003153 FAT-BC, 101020641 PancObese, 748944 LiSDMA, 852086 AGEMEC, 894001 Pept-AGE, 678732 PROMISS, 639382 aCROBAT, 674760 platinDx, 852761 ONco-Energetics_OFF, 964264 TRANSCAN-3, 715575 Reg-Seq, 874708 TheraLymph all OUT on their best chunk (obesity/adiposity, diabetes, sarcopenia, senior malnutrition, brown fat, chemotherapy prediction, tumour bioenergetics, funding coordination, T2D genomics, lymphedema - none about cachexia). Completeness sweep, three non-embedding queries: (a) objective/title ILIKE cachexia|cachectic|wasting syndrome|muscle wasting|tumour-induced weight loss -> 12 projects, (b) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser ILIKE cachexia|cachectic -> 7 projects (639548, 677006, 694677, 741888, 787041, 818943, 949017), (c) cancer/tumour objectives crossed with weight loss|body wasting|adipose tissue loss|fat loss|lean body mass|muscle atrophy or report wasting-of-muscle phrases -> 6 projects, of which 679173 FAT NKT (iNKT cells and obesity), 749978 MATESI (dysphagia) and 814638 GDS (a non-surgical weight-loss sleeve for obesity) were unseen and all read OUT. Every hit across the three sweeps was adjudicated; no satisfying project outside gold. The independent critic's corpus-exhaustive regexp over objective||title||summary||workPerformed||finalResults||teaser for 'cachex|cachect' returned exactly 9 projects corpus-wide, every one of them already adjudicated here, which closes the gold set. term_style exact-term: the question reuses 'cachexia', 'wasting', 'adipose tissue' and 'muscle', all verbatim in both gold texts, and both gold projects are found by lexical (ranks 1 and 4), which is consistent with real term overlap.

text: Several EU-funded projects are working towards next-generation optical and nuclear clocks. For the ones whose clock work is referenced to a specifically named element, isotope or ion species (one or more), which projects are they and which species is each clock referenced to?
reference_answer: Nine projects tie their clock work to named reference species, in three families. Strontium dominates the neutral-atom optical clocks: Mobiclock develops a mobile optical lattice clock on strontium atoms, iqClock's prototype is a field-ready strontium optical clock, and Q-Sense's space optical clock demonstrator (SOC2) is based on cold Sr atoms; TICTOCGRAV works on optical clocks referenced to two species, ultra-cold cadmium (Cd) and strontium (Sr). A second family replaces the electron-shell transition with the low-energy nuclear isomer of Thorium-229: nuClock, ThoriumNuclearClock, CRYSTALCLOCK (a readout scheme for a solid-state 229Th clock) and RaDTho (measuring that isomer's radiative decay towards a nuclear frequency standard). FunClocks references its optical clocks to highly charged ions, naming Ar13+, on which it operated a clock, and highly charged calcium ions used for isotope-shift spectroscopy.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-56 (9 projects whose objective/title contains 'optical clock'); the question was composed after reading their text. Membership test, stated in the question and applied identically to every project: the project's own text ties its clock work to at least one named element, isotope or ion species. Naming a species is the test; the NUMBER of species is not - a project referencing one species and a project referencing two are both in, and the answer field carries the multiplicity. The test is also about what the clock is referenced TO, never about how far the project got, so plans, components and completed work are treated alike. IN: 707864 Mobiclock (strontium optical lattice clock); 820404 iqClock (field-ready strontium optical clock); 772126 TICTOCGRAV (cadmium AND strontium optical clocks - two named species); 691156 Q-Sense (report workPerformed: 'Space Optical Clock (SOC2): It is based on cold Sr atoms'); 856415 ThoriumNuclearClock (Th-229 isomer); 664732 nuClock (clock based on a nuclear transition in Thorium-229); 882708 CRYSTALCLOCK (readout for a solid-state 229Th nuclear clock); 101026762 RaDTho (thorium-229 isomer characterisation towards a nuclear clock/frequency standard); 101019987 FunClocks (highly charged ions, naming Ar13+ and highly charged calcium ions). OUT with reasons - every one names NO species tied to a clock, or no clock: 757386 quMercury - laser cooling and isotope-shift spectroscopy of Hg-199 for an EDM measurement, with Hg lattice clocks named only as a downstream beneficiary of its technologies; 860579 MoSaiQC - builds portable and superradiant clock modules but names no element, isotope or ion species anywhere in its own prose (strontium-88 appears only inside listed publication titles); 820393 macQsimal - workPerformed names 'the miniature atomic clock' but no species; 795121 photonicIons - applied atomic spectroscopy on trapped ytterbium and calcium ions to search for a fifth fundamental force, named species but no clock; 965124 FEMTOCHIP - chip-scale femtosecond laser enabling clocks, no species; 851758 TeLSCombe, 853522 REFOCUS, 727493 ULTRASTABLE - frequency combs, no clock species; 731107 CLONETS, 951886 CLONETS-DS - clock distribution networks, no species; 801285 PIEDMONS, 699387 NAVISAS, 750017 QUESCA, 648575 LIVIN, 949119 CoMoFun - clocks named only as an application of ion traps/cold atoms/molecules, no clock of their own; 832219 ANDLICA, 661171 SYMULGAS, 682629 TOPSIM, 803047 LaGaTYb - ultracold Sr/Yb quantum-simulation projects that name a species and mention clocks only as motivation; 742247 XUV-COMB, 670168 NEWPHYS-MOLECULES - precision spectroscopy of He+/H2, not a clock; remaining pooled hits (714118 TRAPLAB, 695618 Photonis, 844829 RAPTOR, 824096 RADIATE, 861198 LISA, 661777 MagicTin, 818744 INITIUM, 864792 OXYGEN, 892383 RESCATA) are off-topic trap/isotope/geoscience work. Completeness sweeps (non-embedding, run_sql, drafter): (a) objective/title 'optical clock' -> the 9 seed projects; (b) objective/title clock|frequency standard|clock transition -> 43 rows, all adjudicated (most are circadian/biological clocks, combs or networks); (c) clock-word AND element-name over objective -> 10 rows (the 9 gold-candidate seeds plus ANDLICA); (d) report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults containing optical|nuclear|lattice|ion clock -> 27 rows, which is how Q-Sense entered gold and which surfaced SYMULGAS/TOPSIM/LaGaTYb/ULTRASTABLE, all read and rejected. Independent critic sweeps (clock vocabulary x element names over objective+title, and the same over report_text summary/workPerformed/finalResults/teaser) plus full reads of macQsimal, LASERLOOP, OrbiDynaMIQs, QED-PROTONSIZE and photonicIons found no tenth gold member. term_style exact-term: the question reuses the gold texts' own vocabulary ('optical clock', 'nuclear clock', 'isotope', 'ion'), and gold is found by the lexical condition alone (FunClocks lexical rank 1, nuClock 2, ThoriumNuclearClock 5). Retrieval note (LOW, recorded not acted on): at k=10 no single condition surfaces more than 6 of the 9 gold on this phrasing; the critic showed this is phrasing, not corpus - its reformulation 'cadmium and strontium optical clocks combined with atom interferometry to test gravity' put TICTOCGRAV at rank 1 in all four conditions, Mobiclock 3/5/3/3 and Q-Sense 9/4/4/2, and the union of two reformulations reaches 9 of 9 gold.

text: How do EU-funded research projects go about explaining what decides which role an individual ends up taking inside an insect colony?
reference_answer: Seven projects treat the assignment of roles inside an insect society as the thing to be explained, and they attack it at very different levels. Genomic and molecular work dominates: RoyalMess searches for the genes that fate a Messor ant embryo to become a queen or a worker under social hybridogenesis; MELCA uses the double-clonal longhorn crazy ant Paratrechina longicornis to separate the molecular signatures of sex from those of the queen-versus-worker caste; and CASTECON asks whether inter-caste genetic correlations stop queens and workers from each reaching their own optimal dimorphic phenotype, and whether queens manipulate worker phenotype in their own interests. Physiology and neurobiology supply a second angle: DRiveR tests whether dopamine carries the Queen Mandibular Pheromone (QMP) signal that inhibits ovary activity in honeybee workers, while resiliANT measured the lipid content of individual ants by Nuclear Magnetic Resonance and, with targeted starvation, established a causal relationship between fat content and division of labour. MechAnt takes a mechanical view, tying the cutting ability of differently-sized leaf-cutter workers to the ontogeny of task choice and testing whether leaf-cutter colonies are organised according to ergonomic criteria. Division is the broadest: it asks across species why labour is divided at all, and why species differ in the mechanism used to produce different phenotypes - genetic differences, environmental cues, or random assignment of roles.
notes: Seeds from corpus_profile cp6 seed vector-51 (colony life in social insects); drift check re-ran the seed SQL -> 34, unchanged. Scope rule applied to every candidate: IN iff the project's own text makes the assignment of roles inside an insect society (which individuals reproduce vs. which work, or which workers do which task) the thing being EXPLAINED, rather than a given used to explain something else. IN: 695744 CASTECON (caste dimorphism, queen-worker coadaptation, queens manipulating worker phenotype); 741491 resiliANT (fat content causally linked to division of labour; task preference of ant workers); 750766 MELCA (molecular mechanisms governing queen vs worker caste differences); 752656 DRiveR (QMP/dopamine repression of worker reproduction); 834164 Division (explains why and how labour is divided, incl. an across-species study on insects and the mechanism of role assignment); 851705 MechAnt (ontogeny of task choice of differently-sized workers, adaptive value of physical castes, ergonomic colony organisation); 948688 RoyalMess (genetic caste determination, caste-determining genes). OUT under the same rule: 660976 BrainiAnts (explanandum = brain structure/metabolic cost); 706208 SocParPhenoEvol (phenotypic diversity across parasite/host wasp species); 851523 EPIDEMIC and 771402 EPIDEMICSonCHIP and 802628 DISEASE and 771349 DEFEAT (task role is the explanatory variable for infection risk, not the explanandum); 842592 EvolvAnt and 840185 ConvergeAnt (queen number transitions, a colony-level trait); 893244 Ceratina (evolution of sociality across species); 101024100 TEEPI (transposable elements and Blattodea radiation); 101028937 WASSUP (solitary wasps - no colony members to assign roles to); 770964 ANTSolve (collective transport); 659106 GROUPIND (individual vs group personality in ants and starlings); 850859 ECOLBEH (wild birds); 708832 JHSIGNAL (juvenile hormone receptor, Drosophila); 638873 BeeDanceGap (dance communication); 648032 DBA and 654724 GROUPCOG (algorithmic/pigeon collective cognition); 760342 IoBee, 773921 PoshBee (bee health monitoring); 796025 Mesophotic, 101024448 STASIS (false LIKE hits). Sweeps swept objective AND report_text (teaser/summary/workPerformed/finalResults), not objective alone. term_style=paraphrase: the question uses none of the gold texts' distinctive vocabulary (division of labour, caste, eusocial, queen, worker, polyethism, QMP); 4 of the 7 gold projects appear in no condition's top-20. Marginal members disclosed: 834164 Division (insects are one work package; its reported final results are bacterial) and 741491 resiliANT (headline aim is resilience, but its reported work makes task preference the explanandum).
